articles.title: HAL and Samtel inaugurate facility of India's first public-private defence avionics JV in Gurugram
articles.content: ANI Photo | HAL and Samtel inaugurate India’s first public-private defence avionics facility in Gurugram Samtel HAL Display Systems Limited (SHDS), a joint venture between Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Samtel Avionics, officially opened a new manufacturing facility at Udyog Vihar, Phase IV, Gurugram, advancing indigenisation in India’s defence avionics sector. The inauguration was conducted by HAL Chairman and Managing Director Ravi K. SHDS is recognised as the first public-private joint venture in India’s defence avionics industry to indigenously design, qualify and serially produce multifunction displays (MFDs) for fighter aircraft. Add TNM on Google The new facility includes testing and quality assurance capabilities for advanced display systems and supports the design, development, manufacture and product support of display systems for both airborne and ground applications. At the event, Ravi K emphasised that the facility represents a significant step forward in HAL’s efforts to enhance indigenous defence avionics capabilities. He described it as a collaboration combining HAL’s military aviation expertise with Samtel’s display technologies. He affirmed HAL’s commitment to working with Indian industry to accelerate indigenisation, reduce import dependence and provide dependable avionics solutions to the armed forces. ADVERTISEMENT Puneet Kaura, Director of SHDS and Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Samtel Avionics, stated that the facility is the result of nearly 20 years of collaboration with HAL to indigenise technology previously reliant on imports. He pointed to the joint venture’s MFD installed on the Su-30 MKI fighter as evidence that Indian industry can produce defence-grade avionics displays. Established nearly two decades ago, SHDS expects to achieve its highest-ever annual turnover of approximately ₹200 crore this year, making it one of the most successful joint ventures in the HAL group. With a growing order book, the company anticipates this figure could increase to ₹400-500 crore over the next three to four years as new projects commence. SHDS displays are currently fitted on the Su-30 MKI. The joint venture has been selected for HAL’s Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) programme and is involved with the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) programme while exploring opportunities on the Light Utility Helicopter (LUH). Discussions on the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) programme are ongoing, and the company is also pursuing opportunities related to HAL’s Indian Multi-Role Helicopter (IMRH) programme. ADVERTISEMENT SHDS was established in 2006 and is part of the four-decade-old Samtel Group, one of India’s largest integrated display manufacturers. The company holds an industrial licence from the Ministry of Defence, is a CEMILAC-approved design house and a DGAQA-approved manufacturing facility, and complies with ISO 9001:2008 and AS 9100C quality standards.
